lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing, Python
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Decide whether the résumé is aimed at product or operations roles and make its positioning consistent.
items.because: The mix of experience and projects could leave the intended direction unclear.

items.says: Make the diesel-mechanic role’s connection to the target role clear.
items.because: Its placement immediately after the MBA may prompt questions about your direction.

items.says: Clarify whether under five days is a typical result, target, or maximum, and which jobs it covers.
items.because: The turnaround-time measure’s scope is unclear.

items.says: Show what the turnaround time improved from, if possible.
Add a substantiated result of the maintenance or inspection work.
items.because: The bullet reads mainly as a list of duties.

items.says: Consider whether this bullet earns space for the role being pursued.
items.because: It gives duties without an outcome.

items.says: Clarify the pilot region if useful.
Make sure the shorter time to first payment can reasonably be attributed to the redesign.
items.because: The bullet presents the reduction as a result of that change.

items.says: Include whether the checkout result was statistically reliable, if available.
Reconcile shipping the checkout change to all merchants with the later rollout to two more regions.
items.because: The rollout sequence and scope are unclear.

items.says: Clarify whether the Reach score used standard RICE or an adaptation.
items.because: Support tickets closed may be a proxy, but standard Reach estimates users or events affected over a defined period.

items.says: Show what the RICE prioritization led to.
items.because: The bullet does not give a result of the prioritization.

items.says: State the decision or result that followed the interviews and business case.
items.because: The long sequence of activities has little visible outcome beyond selecting a priority.

items.says: Consider whether this and the RICE bullet are separate accomplishments.
items.because: They may overlap.

items.says: Keep the A/B-test-method bullet only if its experiment design demonstrates a distinct skill.
items.because: It largely repeats the checkout-conversion accomplishment.

items.says: Check whether session-level randomization and the analysis support the reported conclusion.
items.because: Repeated sessions from the same user can affect interpretation.

items.says: Clarify what was actually measured by the phrase about an effect on merchants’ customers.
items.because: That phrase is unclear.

items.says: Make the regions and rollout status consistent with the earlier checkout bullet.
items.because: The earlier bullet says the change was shipped to all merchants.

items.says: Distinguish an onboarding rollout from a checkout rollout if the funding refers to onboarding.
items.because: The relationship between the two rollout claims is unclear.

items.says: Clarify whether the late-delivery change is in percentage points.
Explain how the scorecards informed contract renegotiations, if possible.
Specify the measurement period or baseline for the 30% reduction.
Clarify who trained the 45 pickers.
items.because: The reference to retrained pickers is ambiguous.

items.says: Remove the inconsistent first-person possessive.
items.because: The other bullets use résumé-style phrasing.

items.says: Specify the forecast-error measure, if relevant.
Clarify whether the change from 18% to 11% is in percentage points or uses another calculation.
Prioritize the most important contribution rather than combining so many activities.
items.because: The tool rollout, SOPs, training, negotiations, and savings make the bullet crowded and can obscure the main contribution.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1,800 hours saved is measured or projected.
Explain how the time savings were attributed to the rollout.
Distinguish students who could access the app from those who used it, if the numbers differ.
Make the first-year measurement of the nine tonnes clear and ensure the quantity is documented.
The weekly-active-user growth percentage is wrong: 400 to 1,150 is a 187.5% increase, not 150%.
Clarify the time period for the weekly-active-user comparison.
Do not imply the interviews alone caused the full increase without support.
items.because: The interviews support the product decision, but not necessarily that attribution.

items.says: The fill-rate change is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: It rose from 75% to 95%.

items.says: Clarify the time period for the fill-rate change.
Clarify whether the volunteer shift system was the main driver of the fill-rate change.
Distinguish projected annual savings from savings already realized.
items.because: The $2.4M figure comes from a model.

items.says: Clarify your role in sizing the savings opportunity.
Give the assumptions behind the savings estimate, if relevant.
Use active phrasing and identify your contribution to the intake work.
items.because: The bullet is passive.

items.says: Give a measurable effect of the shortened form if evidence is available.
items.because: The bullet lacks a measurable result.

items.says: Be more specific about the extent of front-desk adoption.
items.because: “Adopted by front-desk staff” does not show how widely it was adopted.

items.says: Clarify whether pilot approval and the earlier pilot funding were distinct decisions or stages.
items.because: The final-presentation bullet overlaps with the savings-model bullet.

items.says: Check whether the product-skills list reflects skills and tools used in the strongest bullets.
Place Python consistently with the other technical skills.
items.because: It currently sits under “Product.”

items.says: Indicate Python proficiency only if it can be supported.
Consider adding other role-relevant tools used meaningfully.
items.because: The tools list is short.

items.says: Adjust the visual emphasis to the target role.
items.because: Product applications should foreground the internship and product project, while operations applications should foreground the Crestline results.
